findings.rationale: Local performance of the global model on MN is far below normal (AUC 0.563, z=-7.8; ECE z=+7.9) and its observed prevalence (0.2695) is almost double the model's mean prediction (0.1295), giving CITL -0.14 (z=-9.7). Its subgroup O/E ratios are about 2 in both sex groups, so positives look over-recorded relative to features. Updates are aligned with the federation in rounds 1-2 (cos 0.87-1.0) and point against the median from round 3 onward, with norm ratio growing steadily to about 8. Local data is abnormal, so this reads as flipped labels training the client away from consensus rather than poisoning with normal local data.

CT has the same signature. Local AUC is 0.574 (z=-7.3), ECE is 0.158 (z=+9.0), and observed prevalence (0.2716) is about double the model's mean prediction (0.1347), giving CITL -0.137 (z=-9.4). Subgroup O/E ratios are about 2 in both sex groups. Updates are aligned in rounds 1-2 (cos 0.69-0.86) and opposed from round 3 onward, with norm ratio rising to about 5.6.

VT shows the same pattern. Local AUC is 0.559 (z=-7.6), observed prevalence is 0.2457 against a mean prediction of 0.1285 (CITL -0.117, z=-8.1), and subgroup O/E is about 2.1 in sex group 0. Updates are aligned in rounds 1-2 (cos 0.95 and 0.69), opposed from round 3 onward, and the norm ratio grows to about 5. Smaller client (n=1057 test, 3170 train) but the effect is consistent across tools.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then confirmed suspects with per-client queries. Three clients (CT, MN, VT) stand apart on several independent tools with the same signature: aligned updates in rounds 1-2, opposed updates from round 3 with growing norms, local AUC about 0.56-0.57, observed prevalence about double the predicted risk (CITL about -0.12 to -0.14), and subgroup O/E about 2. Because local data and performance are abnormal, I classed these as label_noise rather than poisoning, with onset round 3. No drift, missing-artefact, prevalence-only, or subgroup-bias faults were confirmed. Some small clients (GU, VI) show noisy feature-tail or drift outliers, but these are not consistent across tools and sit within what small-sample noise would produce, so I did not report them. The budget is fully spent (0 left).
